v: New, unwrapped gifts for children in families facing homelessness. Shop their wish list, give money, or run a drive at your school or workplace (register groups in advance). Deliver or ship by Dec 9.

n: Toys for Tots and KIRO 7 Cares Toy Drive
v: New, unwrapped toys. Confirm drop-off sites and appointment rules with the local coordinator. Most needed in 2025: baby items and gifts for ages 9-13. Fred Meyer service desks took toys in 2025.

loc: Parks across Seattle; pick a site on the sign-up calendar
v: Plant native trees and shrubs to kick off planting season. All ages, no experience needed. Sign up ahead because sites fill.

n: Full Life Care holiday card making meetup
v: Handcraft holiday cards for the community. Family friendly, good for groups.

sch: Giving trees and barrels go out Nov 9. Sponsorship and donation deadline Dec 7.
v: Gifts for kids from infancy to age 18 in North Seattle families with low incomes. Sponsor a child, give gift cards, or donate money. Giving-tree businesses: Math 'n' Stuff, Kaffeeklatsch, Hellbent Brewing, Lake City Autoworks, both Cafe Javasti locations. Barrels: Math 'n' Stuff (8926 Roosevelt Way NE), Kaffeeklatsch (12513 Lake City Way NE, Suite H), Lake City Autoworks (2825 NE 120th St), WaFd Bank (7334 35th Ave NE), Rudy's Barbershop (3620 NE 45th St), Maple Leaf Lutheran Church (10005 32nd Ave NE). Wish list and volunteer sign-up expected in November.

n: Puget Sound Fire Toys for Joy
loc: Any of 17 fire stations (Covington, Kent, Maple Valley, SeaTac, Tukwila and more)
v: New, unwrapped toys for ages 0-12, plus gift cards and money. Online donations open Nov 6 or later on the department's Toys for Joy 2026 page.

n: SnoCope Credit Union Christmas House Toy Drive
v: Take a gift tag from the tree and return the present unwrapped, or give cash at a teller. Benefits kids and teens in Snohomish County. Teens are the biggest need: art supplies, sports balls, headphones, Lego sets, personal-care items.

Free to visit. 32nd year. Benefits Breakthrough T1D (type 1 diabetes research). Donations welcomed per 2025 coverage. Volunteers manage lines and hand out candy canes (Breakthrough T1D chapter listing).

loc: Green Lake Park (bib pickup at the softball fields)
v: Bring canned food to bib pickup to donate. About $27.50 to enter. I did not find which charity gets the food, so check the event page.

n: Full Life Care Thanksgiving doorstep delivery
a: Beacon Hill pickup; deliver in Seattle and King County
v: Deliver a Thanksgiving meal to the door of an isolated older adult. Done in a day.

sch: Volunteer listing shows Nov 28-29 and Dec 4-6. Partial shifts often available.
v: Volunteer roles help run the train days. Ages 13+, background check. Ride tickets sell out (Yuletide Express showed sold out for Dec 4, 11 and 18, $30 each). Volunteers assist with guest flow and activities.
Deliver cookie boxes to local housing communities. Done in a day.

loc: MULE Expedition Outfitters, 30200 SE 79th St, Unit 130, Issaquah
v: Bring a new, unwrapped toy. Benefits Seattle Children's Polar Place Market, where families pick gifts for kids spending the holidays in the hospital. Santa photos, food trucks, live music and a raffle.

loc: Gas Works Park, 2101 N Northlake Way
v: Wear holiday gear. Dogs and strollers welcome. Raises money for the Arthritis Foundation. Listed at $55 for 5K and $70 for 12K. Organizers say details are still being finalized. Volunteers needed Dec 13, 5:00-11:30am, for setup and registration. Training provided, good for groups.
Online supply wish list, plus gifts to the Help the Animals Fund. Volunteer dog walkers apply through the shelter's volunteer program.

Deliver meals to homebound older adults, or make friendly calls to collect orders. Contact 206-448-5767 or mealsonwheels@soundgenerations.org. They also ask for new grocery-size paper bags with handles.

sch: 5-hour shifts, weekdays and weekends. Orientation at 10am.
v: Help make about 2,365 community meals a day. No kitchen experience needed. You stand on a hard floor for the shift. Weekend listing is 18+. Sign up ahead and cancel if you cannot come.
Groups of 3-7 prep, cook and serve a hot meal to neighbors experiencing homelessness.

sch: Classes run 4-8 weeks, 2-3 hours a week, in person or virtual
v: Assist in free art classes for adults recovering from homelessness, addiction and other trauma. Fill out their volunteer interest form.

n: Project Canis: make toys for shelter animals
sch: Any time, done in a day
v: Make toys for shelter animals at home. Family friendly, good for groups. Check Project Canis for what materials and where to send the finished toys.

n: Issaquah Food & Clothing Bank Holiday Gifts Program
v: Gift cards so parents and caregivers can pick gifts for kids 18 and under. Some of the page still shows 2025 details, so confirm.

loc: Mail to 10855 Silverdale Way NW #2224, Silverdale, WA 98383
v: Brand-new toys for hospitalized kids ages 2-16. Youth-led nonprofit.
